title: Quantum numbers
group: CHEM-ATOM / CHEM-PER — Atoms & the Periodic Table
examples: How do the quantum numbers relate to the shape of an orbital?
Can you show me an example of filling orbitals using these rules?
What happens if I try to assign quantum numbers that don't fit the rules?

explain.say: Today we are learning about quantum numbers. These numbers describe electrons in an atom. They help us know where electrons are located.

draw.text: Quantum Numbers: n, l, ml, ms

explain.say: The first number, n, is the principal quantum number. It tells us the main energy level. The value of n must be a positive whole number.
The second number, l, is the azimuthal quantum number. It describes the shape of the orbital. Its value can be any whole number from zero up to n minus one.
The third number, ml, is the magnetic quantum number. It specifies the orbital's orientation in space. Its value ranges from negative l to positive l.
The last number, ms, is the spin quantum number. It describes the electron's spin. This value can only be plus one half or minus one half.
The Pauli exclusion principle states no two electrons in an atom can have the same four quantum numbers. This keeps electrons unique.

draw.text: Pauli: No two electrons same set

faq.q: What does the principal quantum number, n, actually represent?
faq.a: It represents the main energy level or shell the electron occupies. A higher value of n means higher energy.
asks: What is the main energy level?
Does n tell me how much energy it has?

faq.q: How does the value of l limit the possible values for ml?
faq.a: The value of l determines the number of orbitals available in that subshell. ml can only go from negative l to positive l.
asks: Is ml always related to l?
If l is 1, what are the possible ml values?

faq.q: What does the Aufbau principle help us predict?
faq.a: It predicts the order in which electrons will fill the available atomic orbitals. Electrons fill the lowest energy orbitals first.
asks: How do I fill orbitals correctly?
What is the order of filling orbitals?

faq.q: If I use Hund's rule, what am I making sure of?
faq.a: Hund's rule states that electrons will occupy separate orbitals within a subshell before pairing up. This maximizes the total spin.
asks: Why do electrons spread out first?
What is the rule about filling degenerate orbitals?

faq.q: Can I assign quantum numbers if the electron is in a molecule?
faq.a: Quantum numbers are primarily used to describe electrons within isolated atoms. Molecular orbital theory handles bonding differently.
asks: Are these numbers only for atoms?
Do these rules change when atoms bond together?

facts: The principal quantum number, n, can be any positive integer.
The azimuthal quantum number, l, determines the subshell type (s, p, d, f).
The Pauli exclusion principle limits each orbital to two electrons with opposite spins.
The Aufbau principle dictates filling from lowest energy to highest energy.

quiz.say: For an electron in the n=3 shell, what is the maximum possible value for l?
quiz.why: The value of l can go up to n minus one, so 3 minus 1 equals 2.

wrong.0: This is only one possible value; l can be larger if n is large enough.
wrong.2: You might think l can equal n, but it cannot exceed n minus one.
wrong.3: This is too low; l can take several values depending on n.

quiz.say: Which set of quantum numbers is impossible for an electron?
quiz.why: The value of l cannot be greater than n minus one, so l=3 is impossible when n=2.

wrong.0: The magnetic number ml cannot be larger than the value of l.
wrong.2: You might confuse ml with l, but ml must be between -l and +l.
wrong.3: The first shell only allows l=0, which means only s orbitals exist.

quiz.say: If you are filling the next orbital after filling the 2p orbitals, which principle guides you?
quiz.why: The Aufbau principle tells us to fill the next lowest energy orbital available, which is the 3s orbital.

wrong.1: The Pauli principle only concerns the uniqueness of electrons already placed.
wrong.2: Hund's rule only applies when filling orbitals of the same energy level.
wrong.3: This is a general concept, not the specific rule for filling order.
